references.text: Notes that Abram took Sarai as his wife, providing background for the family relationship that Abraham explains in more detail in 20:12.
Abraham asks Sarah to say she is his sister to protect himself—a half-truth, since she was actually his half-sister.
Abraham says about Sarah: "She is my sister", which he then explains and nuances in verse 12.
The Mosaic Law later forbids sexual relations with a half-sister, showing that Abraham's marriage took place before this legislation.
Explicitly forbids marriage with a half-sister (daughter of your father), the same family relationship Abraham describes between himself and Sarah.
A curse on anyone who lies with his sister, emphasizing that such relationships were later forbidden in Israel.
This is a direct continuation of the same event where Abimelech confronts Abraham about the lie concerning their sibling relationship.
